# MCP tool catalog

The abox MCP server offers **24 tools**. This page is generated from the tool definitions in the code (the zod input schemas, the annotations and the documentation each tool carries), so it cannot drift from what `tools/list` returns. The prose around the tools, the approval flow and the limits are in the [MCP server reference](mcp.md); the error codes are in the [error catalog](errors.md).

- Every tool returns `structuredContent` `{ ok, message, ... }` with `snake_case` keys; fields that end in `_at` are ISO timestamps. A failure is `ok: false` with a `code` and `isError: true` (see the [error envelope](errors.md#error-envelope)).
- `pending_approval` is `ok: false` **without** `code` and without `isError`: a human has to decide, see [approval flow](mcp.md#approval-flow-for-agents).
- Unknown parameters are errors (`invalid_input`): every input schema is closed (`additionalProperties: false`), also nested objects.
- **Result** lists the fields of a successful call beside `ok` and `message`; fields that appear only in some cases (such as `hint`) are listed too.

## Tools

### `template_list`

**List templates.** List sandbox templates you may use (language/tooling, isolation, network). Call this first and pick one by its description; never invent a template name. Pass workspace_path (the project you will share) to include that project's own templates from its .sandbox directory; they are marked project=true and need human approval until trusted. A project template named like a built-in one hides it (shadows=[builtin]).

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context defined in `policy.yaml` (never `human`). The answer depends on the caller's own profile.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `templates[]` (`name`, `description`, `use_for`, `backend`, `isolation`, `network_mode`, `usable`, `source`, `project`, `trusted`, `needs_approval`, `shadows`, `allowed`, `backend_available`, `ready`, `not_ready_reason`), `hidden_count`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter        | Type                       | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filter`         | string (at most 100 chars) | no       | Case-insensitive text to match in name, description or use-for.                                                                                                               |
| `all`            | boolean                    | no       | Also list templates your profile does not allow (default: only usable ones).                                                                                                  |
| `workspace_path` | string (1 to 4096 chars)   | no       | Host project path, the same as workspace.path of sandbox_create: also lists the templates of that project (&lt;path&gt;/.sandbox/*.yaml). Must be below your workspace roots. |

### `template_show`

**Show template.** Show one template in detail with the limits that apply to you (resources, network, mounts, TTL). For a template of a project (source=project) pass the same workspace_path as for template_list; trusted says whether a human approved its current content.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context defined in `policy.yaml` (never `human`). The answer depends on the caller's own profile.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `template`, `shadows`, `trusted`, `allowed`, `backend_available`, `capabilities`, `effective_limits`, `warnings`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter        | Type                     | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | string (1 to 64 chars)   | yes      | Template name from template_list.                                                                                                                          |
| `workspace_path` | string (1 to 4096 chars) | no       | Host project path, the same as workspace.path of sandbox_create: also looks for the template in &lt;path&gt;/.sandbox. Must be below your workspace roots. |

### `skill_list`

**List skills.** List skills: SKILL.md folders (task instructions) abox copies read-only into a sandbox at /skills. Add them with sandbox_create skills=[...]; the template's skills come on their own. Lists the skills your profile lets you add (all=true: every one). workspace_path adds the project's .sandbox/skills; those need human approval until trusted.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context defined in `policy.yaml` (never `human`). The answer depends on the caller's own profile.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `skills[]` (`name`, `description`, `source`, `project`, `trusted`, `needs_approval`, `shadows`, `allowed`, `file_count`), `hidden_count`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter        | Type                       | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filter`         | string (at most 100 chars) | no       | Case-insensitive text to match in name or description.                                                                                                                                   |
| `all`            | boolean                    | no       | Also list skills your profile does not let you add (default: only those).                                                                                                                |
| `workspace_path` | string (1 to 4096 chars)   | no       | Host project path, the same as workspace.path of sandbox_create: also lists the skills of that project (&lt;path&gt;/.sandbox/skills/&lt;name&gt;/). Must be below your workspace roots. |

### `skill_show`

**Show skill.** Show one skill: its description, files and the instructions of its SKILL.md. Inside a sandbox that has the skill, the same files are in /skills/&lt;name&gt;/. For a skill of a project pass the same workspace_path as for skill_list.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context defined in `policy.yaml` (never `human`). The answer depends on the caller's own profile.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `skill` (`name`, `description`, `source`, `trusted`, `allowed`, `files`, `sandbox_path`, `front_matter`), `body`, `truncated`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter        | Type                     | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | string (1 to 64 chars)   | yes      | Skill name from skill_list.                                                                                                                                    |
| `workspace_path` | string (1 to 4096 chars) | no       | Host project path, the same as workspace.path of sandbox_create: also looks for the skill in &lt;path&gt;/.sandbox/skills. Must be below your workspace roots. |

### `sandbox_create`

**Create sandbox.** Create an isolated sandbox from a template (without workspace the sandbox starts empty; pass workspace.path to share a project). Pass a fresh request_id so a retry returns the same sandbox. If it answers status=pending_approval, tell the human to approve, then repeat the identical call.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context defined in `policy.yaml` (never `human`). The answer depends on the caller's own profile.
- **Approval:** Depends on the profile's approval mode: always in `strict`; in `medium` and `open` only when the request goes beyond the profile or needs a human (for example a project template nobody approved yet). Waits for the decision up to `limits.approvalWaitMs`, then answers `pending_approval`. Repeat the identical call (same `request_id`) after approval.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, idempotent, reaches beyond the sandbox (network).
- **Result:** `status` (`created`), `idempotent`, `sandbox`, `warnings`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter                              | Type                                                                        | Required               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `template`                             | string (1 to 64 chars)                                                      | no                     | Template name from template_list (default: defaults.template of the config).                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `name`                                 | string (at most 64 chars)                                                   | no                     | Short label (letters, digits, . _ -).                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `host`                                 | string (at most 32 chars)                                                   | no                     | Host id; default local. Only hosts your context allows.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `workspace`                            | object                                                                      | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `workspace.mode`                       | `"mount"` or `"clone"` or `"worktree"` or `"copy"` or `"empty"` or `"sync"` | no                     | worktree\|clone (git, preferred), copy (plain dir), empty, sync, mount (edits the host dir directly!).                                                                                                                                         |
| `workspace.path`                       | string (1 to 4096 chars)                                                    | no                     | Host project path (not needed for empty).                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `workspace.ref`                        | string (1 to 256 chars)                                                     | no                     | Git ref for worktree/clone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `workspace.access`                     | `"ro"` or `"rw"`                                                            | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `workspace.exclude`                    | array of string (1 to 512 chars) (at most 256 items)                        | no                     | Exclude patterns for copy/sync, on top of .gitignore.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `workspace.gitignore`                  | boolean                                                                     | no                     | copy/sync only (an error for other modes): leave out what the project .gitignore files ignore (node_modules, build output, .env). Default true; false copies everything.                                                                       |
| `overrides`                            | object                                                                      | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `overrides.cpus`                       | number (> 0, at most 1024)                                                  | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `overrides.memory`                     | string (at most 32 chars) or number (> 0)                                   | no                     | e.g. "4g" or bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `overrides.ttl`                        | number (> 0) or string (1 to 32 chars)                                      | no                     | Duration string like "2h" or seconds.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `overrides.network`                    | object                                                                      | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `overrides.network.mode`               | `"none"` or `"allowlist"` or `"open"`                                       | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `overrides.network.allow`              | array of string (1 to 260 chars) (at most 256 items)                        | no                     | Extra allowed destinations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `overrides.network.presets`            | array of string (1 to 64 chars) (at most 32 items)                          | no                     | Network presets such as npm, pypi, github.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `overrides.network.private_exceptions` | array of string (1 to 64 chars) (at most 32 items)                          | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `overrides.mounts`                     | array of object (at most 32 items)                                          | no                     | Extra host mounts; usually need approval.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `overrides.mounts[].source`            | string (1 to 4096 chars)                                                    | yes, within its parent |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `overrides.mounts[].target`            | string (1 to 4096 chars)                                                    | yes, within its parent |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `overrides.mounts[].access`            | `"ro"` or `"rw"`                                                            | no                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ttl`                                  | number (> 0) or string (1 to 32 chars)                                      | no                     | Lifetime: duration string like "2h" or seconds (same as overrides.ttl).                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `skills`                               | array of string (1 to 64 chars) (at most 32 items)                          | no                     | Skills from skill_list to copy read-only into the sandbox (/skills/&lt;name&gt;/, index in /skills/INDEX.md, path in $ABOX_SKILLS_DIR), on top of the skills of the template.                                                                  |
| `cache`                                | boolean                                                                     | no                     | false: do not mount the package caches (pnpm store, Cargo registry, ...) the template declares, for a clean install. Default: used when a project is shared (workspace.path) and the policy allows it. You cannot list, read or remove caches. |
| `request_id`                           | string (at most 128 chars)                                                  | no                     | Idempotency key: the same request_id returns the same sandbox. Also used to retry after approval.                                                                                                                                              |

### `sandbox_list`

**List sandboxes.** List your own sandboxes with state and remaining lifetime. Use it to find leftovers to delete.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context defined in `policy.yaml` (never `human`). The answer depends on the caller's own profile.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `sandboxes[]` (the `sandbox` object), `unreachable_hosts`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                                                                                                                    | Required | Description                   |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `state`   | `"requested"` or `"preparing"` or `"created"` or `"running"` or `"stopped"` or `"failed"` or `"expired"` or `"removed"` | no       | Only sandboxes in this state. |

### `sandbox_inspect`

**Inspect sandbox.** Show state, effective limits (what policy granted vs. what the backend reports), network, mounts, skills, TTL, processes, port forwards and pending approvals of one of your sandboxes.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `sandbox` (with `skills[]` when it has some), `processes[]`, `pending_approvals`, `ports[]`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                   | Required | Description                                                           |
| --------- | ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars) | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |

### `sandbox_start`

**Start sandbox.** Resume one of your stopped sandboxes (its workspace and files are kept). Expired sandboxes cannot be started: extend the TTL before it ends (access_request kind ttl) or create a new one.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, idempotent.
- **Result:** `sandbox`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                   | Required | Description                                                           |
| --------- | ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars) | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |

### `sandbox_stop`

**Stop sandbox.** Stop a sandbox (processes end; workspace is kept until sandbox_delete). Prefer sandbox_delete when you are done.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, destructive, idempotent.
- **Result:** `sandbox`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                   | Required | Description                                                           |
| --------- | ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars) | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |

### `sandbox_delete`

**Delete sandbox.** Remove a sandbox and its workspace copy for good. Export results first (sandbox_export). Always clean up when finished, also after errors.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, destructive, idempotent.
- **Result:** `id`, `removed`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                   | Required | Description                                                           |
| --------- | ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars) | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |

### `sandbox_exec`

**Run command.** Run a command in the sandbox and wait for it to finish. Output is capped (~64 KiB per stream) and marked truncated; redirect long output to a file and read it with sandbox_read_file. For servers or long jobs use sandbox_process_start. If a human has taken over the sandbox in a terminal this answers conflict "paused": wait and retry later.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** Only when the profile asks for it: approval mode `strict` or `exec.approval: true`. Waits for the decision up to `limits.approvalWaitMs`, then answers `pending_approval`. Repeat the identical call after approval.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, destructive, reaches beyond the sandbox (network).
- **Result:** `status` (`completed`), `exit_code`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `truncated`, `timed_out`, `duration_ms`, `network`, `network_hint`, `hint`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                                                     | Required | Description                                                                                                            |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars)                                   | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d).                                                  |
| `argv`    | array of string (at most 131072 chars) (1 to 2000 items) | no       | Program and arguments, NO shell (preferred), e.g. ["pnpm","test"].                                                     |
| `cmd`     | string (1 to 262144 chars)                               | no       | Shell command line (run with /bin/sh -c). Use only when you need pipes or redirects; give exactly one of argv and cmd. |
| `cwd`     | string (1 to 4096 chars)                                 | no       | Working directory inside the sandbox.                                                                                  |
| `env`     | object (values: string (at most 32768 chars))            | no       | Extra environment variables. Never put secrets here.                                                                   |
| `timeout` | number (> 0) or string (1 to 32 chars)                   | no       | Seconds or a duration string like "90s", "5m". Capped by policy; a timeout kills the process.                          |
| `stdin`   | string (at most 8388608 chars)                           | no       | Text sent to standard input.                                                                                           |

### `sandbox_process_start`

**Start background process.** Start a long-running process (server, watcher, long build) in the background. Returns process_id; read output with sandbox_process_logs and end it with sandbox_process_stop.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** Only when the profile asks for it: approval mode `strict` or `exec.approval: true`. Waits for the decision up to `limits.approvalWaitMs`, then answers `pending_approval`. Repeat the identical call after approval.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, reaches beyond the sandbox (network).
- **Result:** `status` (`started`), `process_id`, `process`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                                                     | Required | Description                                                                                                            |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars)                                   | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d).                                                  |
| `argv`    | array of string (at most 131072 chars) (1 to 2000 items) | no       | Program and arguments, NO shell (preferred), e.g. ["pnpm","test"].                                                     |
| `cmd`     | string (1 to 262144 chars)                               | no       | Shell command line (run with /bin/sh -c). Use only when you need pipes or redirects; give exactly one of argv and cmd. |
| `cwd`     | string (1 to 4096 chars)                                 | no       | Working directory inside the sandbox.                                                                                  |
| `env`     | object (values: string (at most 32768 chars))            | no       | Extra environment variables. Never put secrets here.                                                                   |

### `sandbox_process_logs`

**Read process logs.** Read output of a background process. Use tail for the last N lines, or since (byte offset = next_offset of the previous call) to read only new output.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for processes of its own sandboxes only.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `process`, `content`, `next_offset`, `size`, `truncated`, `hint`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter    | Type                          | Required | Description                                                    |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `process_id` | string (1 to 64 chars)        | yes      | Process id from sandbox_process_start (p1a2b3c4d).             |
| `since`      | integer (at least 0)          | no       | Byte offset to continue from (next_offset of an earlier call). |
| `tail`       | integer (> 0, at most 100000) | no       | Only the last N lines.                                         |
| `max_bytes`  | integer (> 0)                 | no       | Cap for this call; limited by policy.                          |

### `sandbox_process_stop`

**Stop background process.** Stop a background process started with sandbox_process_start (TERM, then KILL).

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for processes of its own sandboxes only.
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, destructive, idempotent.
- **Result:** `process`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter    | Type                   | Required | Description                                        |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `process_id` | string (1 to 64 chars) | yes      | Process id from sandbox_process_start (p1a2b3c4d). |

### `sandbox_read_file`

**Read file.** Read a file inside the sandbox (paths are sandbox paths; relative paths start at the workspace). Large files are cut at max_bytes and marked truncated; binary files come back base64-encoded.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `path`, `size`, `truncated`, `encoding`, `content`, `hint`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter   | Type                     | Required | Description                                                           |
| ----------- | ------------------------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | string (1 to 64 chars)   | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |
| `path`      | string (1 to 4096 chars) | yes      | Path inside the sandbox.                                              |
| `max_bytes` | integer (> 0)            | no       | Default 64 KiB; limited by policy.                                    |

### `sandbox_write_file`

**Write file.** Write a file inside the sandbox (sandbox paths only; creates or overwrites). Never write secrets. Use encoding=base64 for binary content. Up to 8 MiB of content per call; for bigger files put them in the project workspace or create them inside the sandbox with sandbox_exec. Writes run as the sandbox user: root-owned and abox-managed paths are refused.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, destructive, idempotent.
- **Result:** `path`, `size`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter  | Type                                    | Required | Description                                                           |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`       | string (1 to 64 chars)                  | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |
| `path`     | string (1 to 4096 chars)                | yes      | Path inside the sandbox.                                              |
| `content`  | string (at most 11184812 chars)         | yes      |                                                                       |
| `mode`     | string (pattern `^(?:0o?)?[0-7]{3,4}$`) | no       |                                                                       |
| `encoding` | `"utf8"` or `"base64"`                  | no       | Encoding of content; default utf8.                                    |

### `sandbox_list_dir`

**List directory.** List a directory inside the sandbox (default: the workspace).

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `entries[]` (`name`, `type`, `size`, `mode`, `mtime_ms`; at most 1000), `truncated`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                        | Required | Description                                                           |
| --------- | --------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars)      | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |
| `path`    | string (at most 4096 chars) | no       | Path inside the sandbox; default workspace.                           |

### `sandbox_network_log`

**Network log.** What the egress proxy of one of your allowlist sandboxes allowed and denied, grouped by destination (counts, times, reason). Use it when a download fails or sandbox_exec reports denied network requests. You cannot allow anything yourself: ask with access_request kind=network (details.domains). No request contents, paths or headers.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `mode`, `totals`, `truncated`, `entries[]` (`host`, `port`, `decision`, `allowed`, `denied`, `count`, `first_seen_at`, `last_seen_at`, `reason`, `allowed_now`, ...).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                                   | Required | Description                                                           |
| --------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars)                 | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |
| `since`   | number (> 0) or string (1 to 32 chars) | no       | Only requests from the last N seconds or duration, e.g. "10m", "2h".  |
| `denied`  | boolean                                | no       | Only denied requests.                                                 |
| `limit`   | integer (1 to 200)                     | no       | At most this many destinations, most recent first (default 50).       |

### `sandbox_snapshot`

**Snapshot sandbox.** Save the sandbox state under a name before a risky step. Answers code=unsupported when the backend cannot snapshot; then carry on.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state.
- **Result:** `snapshot_id`, `name`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                   | Required | Description                                                           |
| --------- | ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars) | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |
| `name`    | string (1 to 64 chars) | yes      | Snapshot name (letters, digits, . _ -).                               |

### `sandbox_restore`

**Restore snapshot.** Reset the sandbox to a snapshot (discards changes made since). Pass snapshot_id from sandbox_snapshot (or its name).

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, destructive, idempotent.
- **Result:** `restored`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter     | Type                    | Required | Description                                                           |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | string (1 to 64 chars)  | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |
| `snapshot_id` | string (1 to 256 chars) | no       | snapshot_id returned by sandbox_snapshot.                             |
| `name`        | string (1 to 64 chars)  | no       | Snapshot name, if snapshot_id is not at hand.                         |

### `sandbox_export`

**Export result.** Hand results back: diff or patch (text), branch (git branch abox/... in the source repo) or files (copied to an abox-owned directory). Nothing is applied to the host project. Show it to the human and report every flagged path (CI files, hooks, build scripts).

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, idempotent.
- **Result:** `sandbox_id`, `format`, `content`, `content_lossy`, `branch`, `commit`, `out_dir`, `written`, `files[]`, `flagged[]`, `stats`, `warnings[]`, `truncated`, `hint`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter     | Type                                                   | Required | Description                                                           |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | string (1 to 64 chars)                                 | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d). |
| `format`      | `"diff"` or `"patch"` or `"branch"` or `"files"`       | yes      |                                                                       |
| `paths`       | array of string (1 to 4096 chars) (at most 1000 items) | no       | Only these paths (relative to the workspace).                         |
| `branch_name` | string (1 to 200 chars)                                | no       | format=branch: name; must start with abox/.                           |

### `access_request`

**Request more access.** Ask for more rights for a running sandbox: kind=ttl (details.ttl), resources (details.cpus/memory, up to your limits) or network (details.domains/presets, only for an allowlist sandbox). mount and a new network mode are unsupported on a running sandbox: create a new one. Beyond your profile a human decides; give an honest reason. Do not repeat a pending request; poll with sandbox_inspect.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** A request within the profile's limits is applied (in `strict` mode a human always decides); beyond the profile a human decides. Waits for the decision up to `limits.approvalWaitMs`, then answers `pending_approval`. Do not repeat the call: the change is applied on approval, check with `sandbox_inspect`.
- **Behaviour:** changes state.
- **Result:** `status` (`applied`), `kind`, `sandbox`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter                    | Type                                                 | Required | Description                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                         | string (1 to 64 chars)                               | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d).       |
| `kind`                       | `"network"` or `"mount"` or `"resources"` or `"ttl"` | yes      |                                                                             |
| `details`                    | object                                               | yes      | Fields depend on kind.                                                      |
| `details.mode`               | `"none"` or `"allowlist"` or `"open"`                | no       |                                                                             |
| `details.domains`            | array of string (1 to 260 chars) (at most 256 items) | no       | network: destinations to allow, e.g. ["pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org"]. |
| `details.presets`            | array of string (1 to 64 chars) (at most 32 items)   | no       |                                                                             |
| `details.private_exceptions` | array of string (1 to 64 chars) (at most 32 items)   | no       |                                                                             |
| `details.source`             | string (1 to 4096 chars)                             | no       | mount: host path.                                                           |
| `details.target`             | string (1 to 4096 chars)                             | no       | mount: path in the sandbox.                                                 |
| `details.access`             | `"ro"` or `"rw"`                                     | no       |                                                                             |
| `details.cpus`               | number (> 0, at most 1024)                           | no       |                                                                             |
| `details.memory`             | string (at most 32 chars) or number (> 0)            | no       |                                                                             |
| `details.ttl`                | number (> 0) or string (1 to 32 chars)               | no       | ttl: additional lifetime, e.g. "1h".                                        |
| `reason`                     | string (1 to 4000 chars)                             | yes      | Why you need it. Shown to the human as untrusted text.                      |

### `sandbox_port_forward`

**Forward a sandbox port to the human.** Show the human a dev server running in your sandbox (Vite, Flutter web, php -S): action=add publishes TCP port `port` on 127.0.0.1 of their machine and returns the URL. A human approves by default (pending_approval). Loopback only, no new way out; the server must listen on 0.0.0.0, not just 127.0.0.1. Needs a running sandbox with network allowlist or open (not none); ends when it stops. action=list/remove.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context, for its own sandboxes only (another context's sandbox answers `not_found`).
- **While a human is in the sandbox:** answers `conflict` ("paused") as long as a person has a terminal open in it; nothing is queued, retry later.
- **Approval:** `action=add`: by default a human decides every forward (`ports.allow: ask`); `true` allows it without a question (mode `strict` still asks), `false` denies it. Waits for the decision up to `limits.approvalWaitMs`, then answers `pending_approval`. `list` and `remove` never need approval.
- **Behaviour:** changes state, idempotent.
- **Result:** `add`: `status` (`applied`), `port` (`sandbox_port`, `host_address`, `host_port`, `url`, `target`); `list`: `ports[]`; `remove`: `removed`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type                              | Required | Description                                                                     |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string (1 to 64 chars)            | yes      | Sandbox id as returned by sandbox_create (looks like local/1a2b3c4d).           |
| `action`  | `"add"` or `"list"` or `"remove"` | no       | add (default): open a forward; list: show the open forwards; remove: close one. |
| `port`    | integer (1 to 65535)              | no       | TCP port the server listens on inside the sandbox. Required for add and remove. |
| `reason`  | string (1 to 4000 chars)          | no       | add: why the human should see this port. Shown to the human as untrusted text.  |

### `policy_show`

**Show my limits.** Show the limits of your own profile (templates, resources, network, mounts, TTL, approvals). Read-only; agents cannot change policy.

- **Who may call it:** Any agent context defined in `policy.yaml` (never `human`). The answer depends on the caller's own profile.
- **Approval:** None.
- **Behaviour:** read-only, idempotent.
- **Result:** `context_id`, `owner`, `kind`, `profile`, `allowed_hosts`, `policy` (`content_hash`, `source`, `revision`).

**Parameters:** none.
